name: Disclosure of accounting policies
definition: All significant accounting policies adopted in preparing and presenting financial statements must be disclosed; the disclosure forms part of the financial statements and should normally be given in one place. Disclosure does not cure a wrong treatment.
why_it_exists: The view a set of statements presents can be significantly affected by which policies were chosen, and the choices vary between enterprises. Without disclosure a reader cannot tell whether a difference between two enterprises is a difference in business or a difference in method.
inputs: the set of accounting policies adopted for the period
outputs: a disclosure of all significant accounting policies, forming part of the financial statements, normally in one place
preconditions: financial statements are being prepared and presented
exceptions: UNKNOWN — AS 1 states no exemption from disclosure of a significant policy
common_mistakes: scattering policy notes across several statements, schedules and notes instead of collecting them in one place
presenting the policy statement as supplementary information rather than as part of the financial statements
assuming a disclosed policy legitimises a treatment — AS 1 paragraph 23 says disclosure cannot remedy a wrong or inappropriate treatment
legal_references: UNKNOWN — statutory backing not extracted; only ICAI AS-1 and AS-5 were read for this claim, so no statute is cited
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — AS-1 and AS-5 govern financial-statement policy and period attribution; GST is a separate determination and must not be conflated with it
evidence_required: the policy statement as presented in the financial statements
the location of that statement, to test whether it forms part of the statements
confidence_factors: AS 1 does not define 'significant', so whether a given policy must be disclosed is not decidable from this source alone
weak when only extracted note text is available and its placement within the statements is unknown
validation_checks: every significant accounting policy adopted for the period appears in the disclosure
the disclosure forms part of the financial statements
the significant policies are collected in one place rather than scattered
no incorrect treatment is being justified by the presence of a disclosure
examples: the areas listed in AS 1 paragraph 14 — depreciation method, inventory valuation, goodwill, retirement benefits and others — are ones for which disclosure of the policy adopted will be required
counterexamples: a wrongly valued inventory accompanied by a clear note describing the valuation policy — still wrong; the note does not remedy it

evidence.quote: This Standard deals with the disclosure of significant accounting policies followed in preparing and presenting financial statements.

To ensure proper understanding of financial statements, it is necessary that all significant accounting policies adopted in the preparation and presentation of financial statements should be disclosed.
Such disclosure should form part of the financial statements.
It would be helpful to the reader of financial statements if they are all disclosed as such in one place instead of being scattered over several statements, schedules and notes.
Disclosure of accounting policies or of changes therein cannot remedy a wrong or inappropriate treatment of the item in the accounts.
All significant accounting policies adopted in the preparation and presentation of financial statements should be disclosed.
The disclosure of the significant accounting policies as such should form part of the financial statements and the significant accounting policies should normally be disclosed in one place.
